stem:
A Group 2 metal combines with bromine to form a crystalline solid, $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$.

Excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ is added to a solution of $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$ and a precipitate forms. The mixture is filtered. The precipitate is dried and the mass of the precipitate is recorded.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the formula and colour of the precipitate.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Complete the equation to represent the reaction between $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{AgNO}_3$.

$$\ldots\ldots\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2 + \ldots\ldots\text{AgNO}_3 \rightarrow \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A $0.250\text{ g}$ sample of pure $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$ contains $8.415 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol}$ $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$.

Calculate the relative formula mass, $M_r$, of $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$. Use this to identify $\mathbf{M}$.

Show your working.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: A sample of $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$ is dissolved in water. Chlorine gas is then bubbled into the solution.
parts.text: Describe the observations for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction that occurs when $\mathbf{M}\text{Br}_2$ reacts with chlorine gas.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Compound $\mathbf{Y}$ is a pure **insoluble** solid which contains halide ions.

A single reagent is added directly to compound $\mathbf{Y}$ to determine the halide ion present.

Identify the reagent added. State the observation which would confirm that $\mathbf{Y}$ contains bromide ions.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem: Separate $1.0\text{ g}$ samples of three different magnesium salts are tested in order to identify the anion present in each sample.
parts.text:
Explain how the action of heat is used to identify which sample is:

- $\text{MgCO}_3$
- $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$
- $\text{MgO}$.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: Complete the electron configuration of the magnesium cation present in these salts.

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
A sample of $\text{MgCO}_3\text{(s)}$ is distinguished from a sample of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2\text{(s)}$ by adding a small amount of each solid to $\text{HCl}\text{(aq)}$.

State **one** similarity and **one** difference in these two reactions.
